definitions.explanation: A formal or literary term for the head of government or chief minister. In modern Japanese, used as an elevated synonym for prime minister, or to refer to historical chancellors and chief ministers.

examples.japanese: ⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧{宰相|さいしょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{就任|しゅうにん}→就任：12368_shuunin⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: A new prime minister took office.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{名|めい}{宰相|さいしょう}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{歴史|れきし}→歴史：02267_rekishi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{名|な}→名：03496_na⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{残|のこ}した→残す：01975_nokosu⟧。
examples.english: He went down in history as a great statesman.

examples.japanese: ⟦{国|くに}→国：02204_kuni⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{運命|うんめい}→運命：06879_unmei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{左右|さゆう}→左右：02826_sayuu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧{宰相|さいしょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{決断|けつだん}→決断：13250_ketsudan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、⟦{国民|こくみん}→国民：02757_kokumin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{注目|ちゅうもく}→注目：03483_chuumoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{集|あつ}まった→集まる：01162_atsumaru⟧。
examples.english: The nation's attention was focused on the prime minister's decision, which would determine the country's fate.

notes:
USAGE:
More literary and formal than ⟦{首相|しゅしょう}→首相：03217_shushou⟧ (prime minister) or ⟦{総理大臣|そうりだいじん}→総理大臣：15205_souridaijin⟧. In modern journalism, {宰相|さいしょう} is sometimes used for stylistic variation or to lend gravitas. It also appears when discussing foreign heads of government, particularly historical ones.

Historically, the term referred to the highest-ranking minister in Chinese and Japanese imperial courts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {名|めい}{宰相|さいしょう}: great/renowned statesman
- {宰相|さいしょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{器|うつわ}→器：11838_utsuwa⟧: the caliber to be a leader
- ⟦{鉄|てつ}→鉄：02225_tetsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{宰相|さいしょう}: iron chancellor (often referring to Bismarck)
